paragraphs: Here's what this passage is about, friend: God lives among His people, and that changes how they live together. He says the camp is where He dwells (Numbers 5:3), so the camp matters. The Israelites sent those people outside, and they did just as the LORD had instructed Moses (Numbers 5:4). I think that's a camp that took God being close seriously.

Then the topic turns, and it gets personal. When someone sins against another person, the LORD calls it acting unfaithfully against Him (Numbers 5:6). So wronging your neighbor isn't just a neighbor problem, it's a God problem too, and that should make us all sit up straight, myself included. I have knocked a few cookies off a counter in my day, and I was NOT whistling about it.

So what does God ask for? The guilty person must confess, make full restitution, and add a fifth (Numbers 5:7). Notice the order: say it out loud first, then make it right, and make it more than right. A sorry with no repair is a half-baked cookie, and God wants the whole batch.

Here's the good news to carry with you, baker. When there's no relative to receive the restitution, it goes to the priest along with the ram of atonement, and atonement is made for the guilty person (Numbers 5:8). God doesn't just tell us to fix what we broke, because He makes a way for the one who broke it. So when you've wronged somebody, don't hide and don't hurry past it, but confess, make it right, and trust the God who is close enough to dwell among His people.
